headline: Technology and AI company leaders have been lobbying US health officials in a Slack chat room run by the Medicare agency, KFF Health News reports.
score_reason: Own reporting on thousands of documents with a real open legal question; CMS gave no answers, and the effect on policy is not yet shown.
importance_line: Patients and older Americans who may be steered toward AI health apps are affected first, then the agencies writing the rules and the companies in the chat room, but whether the group breaks advisory-committee law is not settled, and CMS declined to answer questions about it.
summary: KFF Health News reports, after reviewing thousands of Slack messages and meeting recordings, that a Slack workspace run by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) gave companies such as Microsoft, Anthropic, OpenAI, Apple and Google a direct line to health officials, including an invitation to a February FDA session on AI chatbots that was not on the public calendar. A former FDA lawyer told KFF the group resembles a federal advisory committee, which must work in public; CMS declined to answer questions about its legality and calls the effort 'an open, voluntary technical collaboration'.
notes: Full KFF Health News text read. The earlier events (Slack started Aug 2025, FDA session Feb 2026) are background; the reporting is new on 9 Oct 2026.
